# Economic/Political Discussion Board Service Overview

## Service Vision

The Economic/Political Discussion Board is a platform designed to facilitate informed discussions and debates on economic and political topics. Our mission is to provide a space where users can share their insights, exchange ideas, and engage in meaningful conversations about the issues that matter most to them.

## Problem Statement

In today's world, there is a growing need for a platform that allows users to discuss economic and political topics in a respectful and informed manner. Existing platforms often lack the depth and focus required for such discussions, and many are plagued by misinformation and divisive rhetoric. Our service aims to address these issues by providing a platform that fosters informed discussions and promotes a culture of respect and understanding.

## Target Audience

### Primary Users

- **General Public**: Individuals interested in economic and political topics who seek to engage in informed discussions and debates.
- **Economic Analysts**: Professionals who analyze economic trends and policies and wish to share their insights with a broader audience.
- **Political Commentators**: Individuals who comment on political events and developments and wish to share their perspectives with others.

### Secondary Users

- **Moderators**: Individuals responsible for maintaining the platform and ensuring that discussions remain respectful and on-topic.
- **Administrators**: Individuals responsible for the overall management and operation of the platform.

## Core Features

### User Authentication

- Users can register and log in to the platform using their email address and password.
- Users can reset their password if they forget it.

### Article Management

- Users can create, edit, and delete their own articles.
- Users can view articles created by other users.
- Users can search for articles based on keywords and topics.

### Comment Management

- Users can add comments to articles.
- Users can edit and delete their own comments.
- Users can report comments that violate the platform's guidelines.

### File and Image Attachments

- Users can attach files and images to their articles and comments.
- Users can view and download files and images attached to articles and comments.

### User Permissions

- **Guests**: Unauthenticated users who can only view public articles and register/login.
- **Members**: Authenticated users who can create, edit, and delete their own articles and comments.
- **Moderators**: Administrators who can manage all articles, comments, and user accounts.

## Success Metrics

- **User Engagement**: The number of active users and the frequency of their interactions with the platform.
- **Content Quality**: The quality and relevance of the articles and comments posted on the platform.
- **User Satisfaction**: The level of satisfaction of users with the platform and its features.
- **Revenue Generation**: The amount of revenue generated from the platform, if applicable.

> *Developer Note: This document defines **business requirements only**. All technical implementations (architecture, APIs, database design, etc.) are at the discretion of the development team.*

# Enhanced Functional Requirements for Economic/Political Discussion Board

## User Authentication

### User Registration

- Users can register with a unique username and password.
- Users must provide a valid email address for verification.
- Users must agree to the terms and conditions during registration.

### User Login

- Users can log in with their username and password.
- Users can log in using social media accounts (optional).
- Users can reset their password if forgotten.

### Account Management

- Users can update their profile information.
- Users can change their password.
- Users can deactivate their account.

## Article Management

### Creating Articles

- Users can create new articles with a title and content.
- Users can add tags to categorize articles.
- Users can attach files and images to articles.

### Editing Articles

- Users can edit their own articles.
- Users can update the title, content, tags, and attachments.

### Deleting Articles

- Users can delete their own articles.
- Moderators can delete any article.

## Comment Management

### Adding Comments

- Users can add comments to articles.
- Users can reply to other comments.

### Editing Comments

- Users can edit their own comments.

### Deleting Comments

- Users can delete their own comments.
- Moderators can delete any comment.

## File and Image Attachments

### Uploading Attachments

- Users can upload files and images to their articles.
- Users can upload files and images to their comments.

### Managing Attachments

- Users can view, download, and delete their own attachments.
- Moderators can manage all attachments.

## User Permissions

### Access Levels

- Guests: Can only view public articles and register/login.
- Members: Can create, edit, and delete their own articles and comments.
- Moderators: Can manage all articles, comments, and user accounts.

### Restrictions

- Guests cannot create or edit articles or comments.
- Members cannot edit or delete articles and comments that are not theirs.
- Moderators have full access to all features and can manage user accounts.

# Economic/Political Discussion Board Requirements Analysis

## Overview

This document outlines the requirements for a simple economic/political discussion board. The system will allow users to create, view, and comment on articles, as well as attach images and files to their posts. The board will have three main user roles: Guest, Member, and Moderator.

## User Roles

### Guest

- **Description**: Users who have not registered or logged in.
- **Permissions**: View articles and comments.

### Member

- **Description**: Registered users who can create, view, and comment on articles.
- **Permissions**: Create, view, and comment on articles. Upload images and files to articles.

### Moderator

- **Description**: Users with administrative privileges.
- **Permissions**: Delete articles and comments. Ban users.

## Functional Requirements

### User Registration

- **Description**: Users can register for an account.
- **Requirements**:
  - Users must provide a username, email, and password.
  - Users must confirm their email to activate their account.

### User Login

- **Description**: Users can log in to their accounts.
- **Requirements**:
  - Users must provide their username and password.
  - Users must be redirected to their dashboard upon successful login.

### Article Creation

- **Description**: Members can create articles.
- **Requirements**:
  - Members must provide a title and content for the article.
  - Members can attach images and files to the article.
  - Articles must be saved and displayed on the board.

### Article Viewing

- **Description**: Users can view articles.
- **Requirements**:
  - Articles must be displayed in a list format.
  - Users must be able to click on an article to view its details.

### Commenting

- **Description**: Members can comment on articles.
- **Requirements**:
  - Members must provide content for the comment.
  - Comments must be saved and displayed under the corresponding article.

### Attachment Management

- **Description**: Members can attach images and files to articles.
- **Requirements**:
  - Members must be able to upload images and files.
  - Uploaded files must be validated for size and type.
  - Attachments must be displayed with the corresponding article.

### Moderator Actions

- **Description**: Moderators can manage the board.
- **Requirements**:
  - Moderators must be able to delete articles and comments.
  - Moderators must be able to ban users.

## Business Model

### Revenue Streams

- **Description**: The discussion board will generate revenue through advertising and premium memberships.
- **Requirements**:
  - Advertisements will be displayed on the board.
  - Premium memberships will offer additional features.

### Cost Structure

- **Description**: The costs associated with running the discussion board.
- **Requirements**:
  - Server costs for hosting the board.
  - Developer costs for maintaining the board.

### Value Propositions

- **Description**: The value that the discussion board provides to users.
- **Requirements**:
  - Users can discuss economic and political topics.
  - Users can share articles and comments.

### Key Partnerships

- **Description**: The partnerships that the discussion board will have.
- **Requirements**:
  - Partnerships with news organizations for content.
  - Partnerships with advertisers for revenue.

### Key Activities

- **Description**: The key activities that the discussion board will engage in.
- **Requirements**:
  - Content moderation to ensure quality.
  - User engagement to increase participation.

### Key Resources

- **Description**: The key resources that the discussion board will need.
- **Requirements**:
  - Servers for hosting the board.
  - Developers for maintaining the board.

### Key Metrics

- **Description**: The key metrics that will measure the success of the discussion board.
- **Requirements**:
  - Number of registered users.
  - Number of articles and comments.
  - Revenue generated from advertising and premium memberships.

## Authentication Requirements

### User Authentication

- **Description**: Users must be authenticated to access certain features.
- **Requirements**:
  - Users must log in to create articles and comments.
  - Users must be redirected to the login page if they are not authenticated.

### Session Management

- **Description**: User sessions must be managed to ensure security.
- **Requirements**:
  - User sessions must be created upon login.
  - User sessions must be destroyed upon logout.
  - User sessions must expire after a period of inactivity.

### Permission Management

- **Description**: User permissions must be managed to ensure security.
- **Requirements**:
  - User permissions must be assigned upon registration.
  - User permissions must be updated upon promotion or demotion.
  - User permissions must be checked before allowing access to certain features.

## Error Handling

### User Registration Errors

- **Description**: Errors that can occur during user registration.
- **Requirements**:
  - Users must be notified if the username or email is already taken.
  - Users must be notified if the password does not meet the requirements.

### User Login Errors

- **Description**: Errors that can occur during user login.
- **Requirements**:
  - Users must be notified if the username or password is incorrect.
  - Users must be notified if the account is not activated.

### Article Creation Errors

- **Description**: Errors that can occur during article creation.
- **Requirements**:
  - Users must be notified if the title or content is missing.
  - Users must be notified if the file or image is invalid.

### Commenting Errors

- **Description**: Errors that can occur during commenting.
- **Requirements**:
  - Users must be notified if the comment content is missing.

### Attachment Management Errors

- **Description**: Errors that can occur during attachment management.
- **Requirements**:
  - Users must be notified if the file or image is too large.
  - Users must be notified if the file or image type is not allowed.

### Moderator Actions Errors

- **Description**: Errors that can occur during moderator actions.
- **Requirements**:
  - Moderators must be notified if the article or comment does not exist.
  - Moderators must be notified if the user does not exist.

## Performance Requirements

### Response Time

- **Description**: The system must respond to user actions within a reasonable time.
- **Requirements**:
  - The system must load articles and comments within 2 seconds.
  - The system must process user actions within 1 second.

### Scalability

- **Description**: The system must be able to handle a large number of users.
- **Requirements**:
  - The system must be able to handle 10,000 concurrent users.
  - The system must be able to scale horizontally to handle increased traffic.

### Availability

- **Description**: The system must be available to users at all times.
- **Requirements**:
  - The system must have an uptime of 99.9%.
  - The system must have a backup and recovery plan in place.

## Security Requirements

### Data Protection

- **Description**: User data must be protected from unauthorized access.
- **Requirements**:
  - User data must be encrypted at rest and in transit.
  - User data must be backed up regularly.

### Access Control

- **Description**: Access to certain features must be controlled.
- **Requirements**:
  - Access to certain features must be restricted to authenticated users.
  - Access to certain features must be restricted to users with the appropriate permissions.

### Audit Logging

- **Description**: User actions must be logged for auditing purposes.
- **Requirements**:
  - User actions must be logged for auditing purposes.
  - Audit logs must be protected from tampering.

## Compliance Requirements

### Data Privacy

- **Description**: User data must comply with data privacy regulations.
- **Requirements**:
  - User data must comply with GDPR and CCPA.
  - User data must be handled in accordance with the Privacy Policy.

### Accessibility

- **Description**: The system must be accessible to all users.
- **Requirements**:
  - The system must comply with WCAG 2.1 standards.
  - The system must be tested for accessibility.

### Localization

- **Description**: The system must be available in multiple languages.
- **Requirements**:
  - The system must support multiple languages.
  - The system must be tested for localization.

## Related Documents

- [00-toc.md](./00-toc.md): Provides an overview of the service and its purpose
- [01-functional-requirements.md](./01-functional-requirements.md): Defines the core features and user needs for the discussion board
- [03-business-model.md](./03-business-model.md): Outlines the business model and strategies for the discussion board

## Constraints

- Must include detailed steps for each user action
- Focus on the user journey from registration to moderator actions
- Include specifications for creating, viewing, and managing articles and comments
- Include specifications for adding and managing attachments
- Include specifications for moderator actions

## Conclusion

This document provides a comprehensive overview of the requirements for the economic/political discussion board. The requirements are designed to ensure that the system is user-friendly, secure, and scalable. The document will serve as a guide for the development team throughout the project lifecycle.

# Economic/Political Discussion Board Business Model

## Revenue Streams

### Advertising

- Display ads on articles and comments.
- Sponsored posts and articles.
- Premium ad placements for key partners.

### Subscription Model

- Free tier with limited features.
- Premium tier with additional features and no ads.
- Enterprise tier for organizations with custom features and support.

### Freemium Model

- Free access to basic features.
- Paid access to advanced features and premium content.

## Cost Structure

### Development Costs

- Initial development and design costs.
- Ongoing development and maintenance costs.

### Operational Costs

- Hosting and server costs.
- Content moderation and support costs.
- Marketing and promotion costs.

### Personnel Costs

- Salaries for development and operations teams.
- Salaries for content moderators and support staff.

## Value Propositions

### Unique Features

- Focus on economic and political discussions.
- Image and file attachments for articles.
- User-friendly interface for easy navigation.

### Benefits

- Platform for informed discussions and knowledge sharing.
- Tools for researchers and analysts to track economic and political trends.
- Community for like-minded individuals to connect and collaborate.

## Key Partnerships

### Content Partners

- Collaborations with economic and political analysts.
- Partnerships with news organizations and research institutions.

### Technology Partners

- Cloud hosting providers for reliable and scalable infrastructure.
- Payment gateway providers for secure transactions.

## Key Activities

### Content Moderation

- Regular reviews and approvals of articles and comments.
- Reporting and removal of inappropriate content.

### User Support

- Providing customer support and troubleshooting assistance.
- Conducting user surveys and feedback sessions.

## Key Resources

### Technology

- Cloud hosting and server infrastructure.
- Development and design tools.

### Personnel

- Development and operations teams.
- Content moderators and support staff.

## Key Metrics

### User Engagement

- Number of active users.
- Time spent on the platform.
- Frequency of visits.

### Financial Performance

- Revenue generated from advertising and subscriptions.
- Cost of acquisition and customer lifetime value.
- Profit margins and return on investment.

## Conclusion

The Economic/Political Discussion Board aims to provide a platform for informed discussions and knowledge sharing. With a focus on economic and political topics, the service offers unique features and benefits to its users. The business model includes revenue streams from advertising and subscriptions, with a cost structure that includes development, operational, and personnel costs. Key partnerships and activities are essential for the success of the service, and key resources and metrics are used to measure its performance.

models.name: economic_political_discussion_board_channels
models.description:
Discussion board channels that organize content into distinct categories.

Channels serve as the primary organizational structure for the discussion board,
providing users with clear categories to navigate and participate in discussions.
Each channel represents a specific topic or theme that users can explore and
contribute to. Channels can contain multiple sections, which further organize
the content within the channel.

The channel entity is a primary entity that users interact with directly,
requiring independent management capabilities. This includes the ability to
create, edit, and delete channels, as well as view and search across all
channels.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: The name of the channel, which is displayed to users and used for identification purposes.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: A detailed description of the channel's purpose and content, helping users understand what the channel is about.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when the channel was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when the channel was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when the channel was deleted, if applicable.

models.name: economic_political_discussion_board_sections
models.description:
Sections within channels that further organize content into subcategories.

Sections provide an additional layer of organization within channels, allowing for
the grouping of related content. Each section represents a specific subtopic or
aspect of the channel's main theme. Sections can contain multiple articles,
which are the primary content items within the discussion board.

The section entity is a primary entity that users interact with directly,
requiring independent management capabilities. This includes the ability to
create, edit, and delete sections, as well as view and search across all
sections within a channel.

and the rules for user participation.

The configuration entity is a primary entity that administrators interact with
directly, requiring independent management capabilities. This includes the
ability to create, edit, and delete configurations, as well as view and search

models.name: economic_political_discussion_board_articles
models.description:
Main article entity for economic/political discussion board.

Contains shared fields for all articles including title, content, and
creation metadata. The actor_type field indicates which user type created
the article (member or moderator).

Articles can have multiple attachments through the
{@link economic_political_discussion_board_attachment_of_articles}
relationship. Comments are associated through the
{@link economic_political_discussion_board_comments} relationship.

Each article is associated with a channel and section for
categorization. Historical versions are tracked through the
{@link economic_political_discussion_board_article_snapshots}
relationship.

Soft deletion is supported through the deleted_at field to allow
content recovery while maintaining audit trails.

plainFields.description: When this article was soft-deleted (null if active).

models.name: economic_political_discussion_board_article_of_members
models.description:
Tracks articles created by members.

Contains member-specific information about articles created by regular
members. Each record links to a specific article and member, recording
the member's session at creation time.

This table establishes the 1:1 relationship between articles and the
members who created them, while the main article table tracks the
shared article data.

The combination of article_id and member_id is unique to ensure
each article is associated with exactly one member.

Contains moderator-specific information about articles created by

discussions.
Each channel represents a specific topic or theme that users can explore and
contribute to. Channels can contain multiple sections, which further
organize
the content within the channel.

requiring independent management capabilities. This includes the ability to
create, edit, and delete channels, as well as view and search across all
channels.

subtopic or

which are the primary content items within the discussion board.

### `economic_political_discussion_board_articles`

Main article entity for economic/political discussion board.

Contains shared fields for all articles including title, content, and
creation metadata. The actor_type field indicates which user type created
the article (member or moderator).

Articles can have multiple attachments through the
[economic_political_discussion_board_attachment_of_articles](#economic_political_discussion_board_attachment_of_articles)
relationship. Comments are associated through the
[economic_political_discussion_board_comments](#economic_political_discussion_board_comments) relationship.

Each article is associated with a channel and section for
categorization. Historical versions are tracked through the
[economic_political_discussion_board_article_snapshots](#economic_political_discussion_board_article_snapshots)
relationship.

Soft deletion is supported through the deleted_at field to allow
content recovery while maintaining audit trails.

Properties as follows:

- `economic_political_discussion_board_channel_id`
  > Channel this article belongs to. {@link
  > economic_political_discussion_board_channels.id}

  > Section this article belongs to. {@link
  > economic_political_discussion_board_sections.id}
- `actor_type`: Type of actor who created this article. Either 'member' or 'moderator'.
- `title`: Title of the article.
- `content`: Main content of the article.
- `created_at`: When this article was created.
- `updated_at`: When this article was last updated.
- `deleted_at`: When this article was soft-deleted (null if active).

Tracks articles created by members.

Contains member-specific information about articles created by regular
members. Each record links to a specific article and member, recording
the member's session at creation time.

This table establishes the 1:1 relationship between articles and the
members who created them, while the main article table tracks the
shared article data.

The combination of article_id and member_id is unique to ensure
each article is associated with exactly one member.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `economic_political_discussion_board_article_id`
  > Article created by this member. {@link
  > economic_political_discussion_board_articles.id}
- `economic_political_discussion_board_member_id`
  > Member who created this article. {@link
  > economic_political_discussion_board_members.id}
- `economic_political_discussion_board_member_session_id`
  > Session used when this article was created. {@link
  > economic_political_discussion_board_member_sessions.id}
- `created_at`: When this article was created by the member.

### `economic_political_discussion_board_article_of_moderators`

Tracks articles created by moderators.

Contains moderator-specific information about articles created by
moderators. Each record links to a specific article and moderator,
recording the moderator's session at creation time.

This table establishes the 1:1 relationship between articles and the
moderators who created them, while the main article table tracks the
shared article data.

each article is associated with exactly one moderator.

- `created_at`: When this article was created by the moderator.

Historical versions of articles for audit trail.

Captures point-in-time states of articles for historical tracking and
audit purposes. Each snapshot records the complete state of an article
at a specific point in time, including all shared fields from the main
article table.

Snapshots are created whenever an article is created, updated,
or deleted. This allows for complete reconstruction of an article's
lifecycle and provides a complete audit trail of all changes.

The relationship to the main article table allows tracking all versions
of each article, while the created_at field records when each snapshot
was taken.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `economic_political_discussion_board_article_id`

- `actor_type`: Type of actor who created this article. Either 'member' or 'moderator'.
- `title`: Title of the article at this snapshot.
- `content`: Content of the article at this snapshot.
- `created_at`: When this snapshot was taken.
- `updated_at`: When this article was last updated at this snapshot.
- `deleted_at`: When this article was soft-deleted at this snapshot (null if active).

### `economic_political_discussion_board_attachments`

Main attachment entity containing shared fields for all attachments.

Stores core attachment information including file metadata, upload
timestamps,
and system management fields. This is the primary entity that users interact
with when managing attachments across the system.

Attachments can be associated with either articles or comments through
subtype entities, creating a polymorphic relationship pattern.

The main entity contains shared fields like file name, size, and MIME type,
while subtype entities track which specific content type each attachment
belongs
to. This structure allows for proper data integrity while supporting
the different content types that can have attachments.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `actor_type`: Type of actor who created the attachment (e.g., 'member', 'moderator').
- `file_name`: Original name of the uploaded file.
- `file_size`: Size of the file in bytes.
- `mime_type`: MIME type of the file (e.g., 'image/jpeg', 'application/pdf').
- `file_path`: Storage path of the file in the system.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the attachment was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when the attachment was last updated.
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp when the attachment was deleted (soft delete).

### `economic_political_discussion_board_attachment_of_articles`

Subtype entity tracking attachments associated with articles.

This table establishes the relationship between attachments and articles,
allowing articles to have multiple attachments while maintaining proper
data integrity. Each record links an attachment to a specific article and
includes the actor who created the attachment.

The subtype pattern ensures that attachments can be properly associated
with articles while maintaining the polymorphic relationship structure
with other content types.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `economic_political_discussion_board_attachment_id`
  > Reference to the main attachment entity. {@link
  > economic_political_discussion_board_attachments.id}
- `economic_political_discussion_board_article_id`
  > Reference to the article this attachment belongs to. {@link
  > economic_political_discussion_board_articles.id}
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this attachment-article relationship was created.

### `economic_political_discussion_board_attachment_of_comments`

Subtype entity tracking attachments associated with comments.

This table establishes the relationship between attachments and comments,
allowing comments to have multiple attachments while maintaining proper
data integrity. Each record links an attachment to a specific comment and
includes the actor who created the attachment.

The subtype pattern ensures that attachments can be properly associated
with comments while maintaining the polymorphic relationship structure
with other content types.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `economic_political_discussion_board_attachment_id`
  > Reference to the main attachment entity. {@link

- `economic_political_discussion_board_comment_id`
  > Reference to the comment this attachment belongs to. {@link
  > economic_political_discussion_board_comments.id}
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this attachment-comment relationship was created.
